issue_context.title: TiDB does not show non default hash partitions in show create table
issue_context.body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

### 1. Minimal reproduce step (Required)

```sql
CREATE TABLE `thash` (
  `id` bigint unsigned NOT NULL,
  `data` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`)
)
PARTITION BY HASH (`id`)
(PARTITION pEven COMMENT = "Even ids",
 PARTITION pOdd COMMENT = "Odd ids");
SHOW CREATE TABLE thash;
SELECT TABLE_NAME,PARTITION_NAME,PARTITION_ORDINAL_POSITION,PARTITION_METHOD,PARTITION_EXPRESSION,PARTITION_DESCRIPTION,PARTITION_COMMENT /*T! , TIDB_PLACEMENT_POLICY_NAME, TIDB_DIRECT_PLACEMENT */ FROM information_schema.partitions WHERE TABLE_NAME = 'thash';
```

### 2. What did you expect to see? (Required)
```sql
mysql> CREATE TABLE `thash` (
    ->   `id` bigint unsigned NOT NULL,
    ->   `data` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
    ->   PRIMARY KEY (`id`)
    -> )
    -> PARTITION BY HASH (`id`)
    -> (PARTITION pEven COMMENT = "Even ids",
    ->  PARTITION pOdd COMMENT = "Odd ids");
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0,02 sec)

mysql> SHOW CREATE TABLE thash;
+-------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Table | Create Table                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
+-------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| thash | CREATE TABLE `thash` (
  `id` bigint unsigned NOT NULL,
  `data` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 COLLATE=utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci
/*!50100 PARTITION BY HASH (`id`)
(PARTITION pEven COMMENT = 'Even ids' ENGINE = InnoDB,
 PARTITION pOdd COMMENT = 'Odd ids' ENGINE = InnoDB) */ |
+-------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
1 row in set (0,00 sec)

mysql> SELECT TABLE_NAME,PARTITION_NAME,PARTITION_ORDINAL_POSITION,PARTITION_METHOD,PARTITION_EXPRESSION,PARTITION_DESCRIPTION,PARTITION_COMMENT /*T! , TIDB_PLACEMENT_POLICY_NAME, TIDB_DIRECT_PLACEMENT */ FROM information_schema.partitions WHERE TABLE_NAME = 'thash';
+------------+----------------+----------------------------+------------------+----------------------+-----------------------+-------------------+
| TABLE_NAME | PARTITION_NAME | PARTITION_ORDINAL_POSITION | PARTITION_METHOD | PARTITION_EXPRESSION | PARTITION_DESCRIPTION | PARTITION_COMMENT |
+------------+----------------+----------------------------+------------------+----------------------+-----------------------+-------------------+
| thash      | pOdd           |                          2 | HASH             | `id`                 | NULL                  | Odd ids           |
| thash      | pEven          |                          1 | HASH             | `id`                 | NULL                  | Even ids          |
+------------+----------------+----------------------------+------------------+----------------------+-----------------------+-------------------+
2 rows in set (0,00 sec)
```
Apart from the MySQL specifics.

### 3. What did you see instead (Required)
```sql
tidb> CREATE TABLE `thash` (
    ->   `id` bigint unsigned NOT NULL,
    ->   `data` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
    ->   PRIMARY KEY (`id`)
    -> )
    -> PARTITION BY HASH (`id`)
    -> (PARTITION pEven COMMENT = "Even ids",
    ->  PARTITION pOdd COMMENT = "Odd ids");
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0,01 sec)

tidb> SHOW CREATE TABLE thash;
+-------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Table | Create Table                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
+-------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| thash | CREATE TABLE `thash` (
  `id` bigint(20) unsigned NOT NULL,
  `data` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`) /*T![clustered_index] CLUSTERED */
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 COLLATE=utf8mb4_bin
PARTITION BY HASH( `id` )
PARTITIONS 2 |
+-------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
1 row in set (0,00 sec)

tidb> SELECT TABLE_NAME,PARTITION_NAME,PARTITION_ORDINAL_POSITION,PARTITION_METHOD,PARTITION_EXPRESSION,PARTITION_DESCRIPTION,PARTITION_COMMENT /*T! , TIDB_PLACEMENT_POLICY_NAME, TIDB_DIRECT_PLACEMENT */ FROM information_schema.partitions WHERE TABLE_NAME = 'thash';
+------------+----------------+----------------------------+------------------+----------------------+-----------------------+-------------------+----------------------------+-----------------------+
| TABLE_NAME | PARTITION_NAME | PARTITION_ORDINAL_POSITION | PARTITION_METHOD | PARTITION_EXPRESSION | PARTITION_DESCRIPTION | PARTITION_COMMENT | TIDB_PLACEMENT_POLICY_NAME | TIDB_DIRECT_PLACEMENT |
+------------+----------------+----------------------------+------------------+----------------------+-----------------------+-------------------+----------------------------+-----------------------+
| thash      | pEven          |                          1 | HASH             | `id`                 |                       | Even ids          | NULL                       | NULL                  |
| thash      | pOdd           |                          2 | HASH             | `id`                 |                       | Odd ids           | NULL                       | NULL                  |
+------------+----------------+----------------------------+------------------+----------------------+-----------------------+-------------------+----------------------------+-----------------------+
2 rows in set (0,00 sec)
```

Here the names are missing from `SHOW CREATE TABLE thash`, but it did record the info as seen in the `information_schema.partitions` table.

### 4. What is your TiDB version? (Required)

<!-- Paste the output of SELECT tidb_version() -->

comments: Also if trying different placement rules like 'PARTITION pEven PRIMARY_REGION = "us-west-1" REGIONS = "us-west-1,us-west-2"' it does not show up in information_schema.partitions, so I'm not sure it is stored or not? Also not sure if that is a separate bug or part of this bug.
Please check whether the issue should be labeled with 'affects-x.y' or 'fixes-x.y.z', and then remove 'needs-more-info' label.

review_comments: I think there should also be a test for '... PARTITION BY HASH (id) PARTITIONS 2' as well as one with named partitions, but with default names like '... PARTITION BY HASH (id) (PARTITION p0, PARTITION p1)', what do you think?
yes, but it already exists in an old case in `executor/seqtest/seq_executor_serial_test.go`, and I fixed it.

Will this not hide something like this:
```sql
PARTITION BY HASH (id)
(PARTITION pOnly COMMENT = 'a single partition')
```

I'm not sure how easy it is to be fully compatible with MySQL, since IIRC it will store the partitioning definition as text, making it easy to check if it is the default 'PARTITIONS N' or all partitioned defined one by one.

I also know it is a bit strange to define each hash partition, since it should be possible to do 'ADD PARTITION' or COALESCE PARTITION' which would simply add (a possible default partition) or drop one or more partitions and redistribute all the rows/data. But as long as we define how TiDB handles these I'm OK with which behaviour we choose.
I.e. differentiate between default 'PARTITIONS N' and define each and every partition
OR always show the definition of each and every partition in the `SHOW CREATE TABLE` output.

yes, that makes me puzzled too, so I chose to show the only partition first, but for compatibility, I hid it then.
IMO, I prefer to list partitions one by one, including the only parition. that make partitions definition more clear.

Hmm, I cannot see any other solution (without changing how PartitionInfo is stored) than check if all hash partitions would be the same as if they were created with 'PARTITIONS N', i.e. Partition name = pN, Comment = "", and PlacementPolicyRef = nil and DirectPlacementOpts = nil.
If implemented like that, then it would also be backwards compatible and the only time it would be inconsistent with MySQL is if you explicitly define all partitions as if they would look by default 'PARTITIONS N'.

I created another PR to cover a bit more: https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/pull/29945
Do you think that PR would cover all this as well?
LGTM, the nested annotation is a problem indeed

I think this is incomplete, it should add all set or non-default table options, not only COMMENT or ENGINE (and also not include them when not set, depending on how strict we want to be compatible with MySQL).
the default name defined before here. the[ test case](https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/pull/29931/files#L532) shows the result
